gallery.caption: The door in the wall, the path beyond it, and the surprise at the end.
gallery.title: The three parts of the garden adventure

gallery.caption: Small, old, and almost covered by ivy.
gallery.title: The green door in the wall

objectives: Follow a journey from a hidden door to the far side of a magic garden.
Name the three parts of the adventure.
Use five new garden words in your own sentences.
Describe what the boy finds at the end of the path.
Retell the adventure to someone else in the right order.
Tell a friend the small lesson at the end.

sections.body:
This is a story about a boy called Bình. His grandmother gave him the house with the old garden behind it. Most days he plays in the front yard and leaves the back alone.

But one wet afternoon he looks over the garden wall and sees something strange. There is a door in the wall. It is green, and small, and almost hidden by ivy.

A good adventure has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning tells you who is going and why. The middle brings the surprise. The end gives you something worth keeping.

This adventure has that shape. At the beginning, Bình finds the door and cannot decide whether to open it. In the middle, he steps through and finds a whole garden on the other side. At the end, the garden gives him something that will change his ordinary days.

Read it slowly. Listen for the small sounds. Then tell the story to someone you trust.
examples: This story is about a door in a garden wall.
A good adventure has a beginning, a middle and an end.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this garden adventure is about

sections.body:
Rain has been falling all afternoon. Bình is looking for something to do.

He goes out to the back of the garden. The grass is wet under his sandals. The old wall runs along the side of the house, made of warm brown bricks with moss in the gaps.

Then he sees the door.

It is set into the wall, and it is green. The paint is old and peeling. Ivy grows across it, and small leaves curl around the handle.

Bình has lived here for two years. He has never seen this door before. The house came with a key for the front and the back. There is no key for this one.

He puts his hand on the handle. It is cold. He pushes a little. The door gives a small click, like a sleepy animal waking up.

Behind the door is a path. The path is made of pale round stones. The stones glow very faintly in the grey afternoon.

Bình looks back at the house. Then he looks at the path. He takes one step, then another, and the door swings shut behind him.
examples: The door was green, with old peeling paint.
Ivy grew across the door and curled around the handle.
He took one step, then another, and the door shut behind him.
sections.heading: The beginning: a green door under the ivy

sections.body:
The rain stops the moment Bình steps through. He does not notice this at first.

The air on the other side smells warm and green, like the inside of a forest after rain. There is no house behind him. There is only the door, and the wall, and the garden he came from on the other side.

He follows the pale stones. They curve between tall green leaves, and every leaf he brushes is cool and damp.

The path leads him to a small clearing. And there is a garden here. Not his grandmother's garden. A different one.

Things grow here that do not grow at home. A tree hangs heavy with fruit the colour of candles. Flowers open only when he looks away. Small silver fish swim in the air above his head, and they make no sound.

Bình sits down on a stone. He is not afraid, exactly. He is more like the person who is trying a new food and does not know yet if they like it.

Then he hears a sound he knows. A small thin sound. Behind the tall leaves, something is crying.

Bình pushes the leaves aside and finds a tiny grey creature, no bigger than his two hands together. It is wet. It is alone. It has lost its way home.
examples: The rain stopped the moment he stepped through.
Silver fish swam in the air above his head.
Behind the leaves, something was crying.
sections.heading: The middle: the garden behind the garden

sections.body:
The little creature has long ears and a soft grey tail. It is a **vole**.

Bình knows voles. They live in the grass at home. But this one is different. Its fur is silver, and it looks at Bình like it understands every word.

He picks it up carefully. It stops crying. It makes a small sound that is almost a laugh.

They walk on together. The path curves downhill to a pool of clear water, and Bình sees something at the bottom. A single golden seed, resting on the stones.

He reaches down and picks it up. It is warm in his hand, even though the water is cold.

Then the garden begins to fade. The leaves go pale. The silver fish drift down. The pool turns grey.

Bình runs back along the pale stones, holding the vole in one hand and the seed in the other. The door is still there. He falls through it into the wet grass of his grandmother's garden, and it swings shut behind him with a soft click.

In his pocket he has a golden seed. In his arms he has a small silver vole. And from that day on, whenever he plants the seed, something wonderful grows.

That is the surprise. He did not go looking for a friend. He found one anyway.
examples: The little creature was a vole with silver fur.
The seed was warm in his hand.
He did not go looking for a friend, and he found one anyway.
sections.heading: The surprise: the seed and the small grey friend

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

An **ivy** is a green plant that climbs up walls and trees. It holds on tightly and does not need much light.

A **clearing** is an open space in the middle of woods, where the trees step back and the sky can reach the ground.

**Ivy-covered** things are hidden by it. A door covered in ivy is easy to walk past a hundred times without noticing.

A **seed** is the small beginning of a plant. Inside a seed is everything the plant needs to begin.

**To plant** means to put a seed into the ground and look after it. Planting is a promise to come back.
examples: Ivy climbs up the wall of the old house.
A seed needs soil and water to grow.
He planted the seed and watered it every morning.
sections.heading: The words inside this story

terms.example: Ivy grew across the green door.
terms.gloss: A green climbing plant that grows up walls and trees. It holds on tightly and hides what is behind it.

terms.example: The path led to a small clearing.
terms.gloss: An open space in the middle of woods, where the trees step back and the sky reaches the ground.

terms.example: He found a golden seed at the bottom of the pool.
terms.gloss: The small beginning of a plant. Inside it is everything the plant needs to start.

terms.example: Bình planted the seed on the first of April.
terms.gloss: To put a seed into the ground and look after it. Planting is a promise to come back.

terms.example: The door was hidden under the ivy.
terms.gloss: Kept out of sight, so that people walk past without noticing.

sections.body:
What did Bình learn? He learned that the best things are often hiding in plain sight. The door was in the garden the whole time, and he walked past it a hundred times.

He also learned that being kind comes first. He did not know the vole. He did not know what to do. He picked it up anyway, and that was enough.

Here is how to tell this adventure to someone. Keep the order, and the surprise will land in the right place.

Start with who is going and why. Tell the hard part in the middle. Save the surprise for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of this adventure is this: open the small door. It may be the door you did not know was there.
examples: The story starts with a boy in a wet garden.
The surprise comes at the very end.
Open the small door, and you may find something wonderful.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start with the character: Bình in the wet garden, looking at the old wall.
Tell the middle: the green door, and the garden on the other side.
Tell the surprise: the silver vole and the golden seed.
End with the lesson: open the small door you did not notice before.

item.summary: A boy finds an old green door in the garden wall and opens it into a garden that should not exist. Follow him past the ivy, through the hidden garden and to the surprise waiting at the end. After reading, you can retell the adventure, use five new garden words in your own sentences, and explain why he keeps the door a secret.
item.title: The Secret Door in the Garden
